mainTopic: Impurity from body folds, from emissions felt or not felt, and from discharges that break loose before a change in status
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: a fold in the body is not 'inside of inside.' ריש לקיש then rules that a זב who moves a pure person with a pole tucked in his body fold does not make him impure, because the תורה ties הסט to the hands, which are on the outside of the body. The גמרא gives פסוקים showing that a זב and a בעל קרי become impure only once the flow leaves the body. It then asks how a כהן may hold his אמה to stop an emission, and אביי and רבא disagree about whether a soft cloth is allowed. שמואל rules that seed which the whole body does not feel does not make a person impure, and the גמרא brings other versions of his rule and the practical difference between them. רבא asks about seed that broke loose with a feeling but came out without one, and the proof the גמרא brings for this is pushed away. Next רבא asks about a גוי who converted, and about a זבה whose urine broke loose before she immersed; both questions end in תיקו. The amud ends as רבא begins another question about a gentile זבה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A body fold is not 'inside of inside'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining what the earlier ruling of רבא comes to teach. A fold in a person's body does not count as 'inside of inside.'
steps.simpleTranslation: …and not 'the inside of its inside.' That is what he comes to teach us.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the tail end of the previous discussion. The גמרא wraps up by saying what the earlier ruling teaches: a body fold is not treated as 'inside of inside.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might have thought a fold in the body is like a hidden inner space inside a vessel, which would change the טומאה rules. The phrase קא משמע לן tells us the ruling was needed to reject that idea. This closes the earlier topic before ריש לקיש opens a new one about body folds.

keyTerms.meaning: The inside of its inside: something enclosed within another thing that is itself inside a vessel
He comes to teach us (the point the ruling was needed for)

phrases.english: and not the inside of its inside —
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from just before this section: we might have thought a body fold counts as an inner hidden space.

phrases.english: this teaches us.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא תּוֹךְ תּוֹכוֹ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the previous discussion, which began before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A fold in the body is not considered 'inside of inside.'

steps.title: ריש לקיש: a pole in the body fold of a זב or of a pure person
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rules on two cases. In the first, a pole is in a זב's body fold and he moves a pure person with it; the pure person stays טהור. In the second, a pole is in a pure person's fold and he moves the זב with it; the pure person becomes טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: If a pole is in the body fold of a זב, and he moves a pure person with it, that person stays pure. If a pole is in the body fold of a pure person, and he moves the זב with it, he becomes impure.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש opens a new topic about body folds. He gives two mirror-image cases with opposite results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a זב makes things impure just by moving them (הסט), even without touching. Yet when he moves something with a pole held in a body fold, nothing becomes impure. In the reverse case, the pure person becomes impure, because a pure person who moves a זב becomes טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: His body fold (such as the armpit or a fold of skin)
A man made impure by a certain bodily discharge; he passes on טומאה in many ways
He moved something without touching it directly

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume both cases follow the same logic. The first case is about the זב doing the moving, which has special limits. The second is about a pure person moving the זב, and he becomes impure whatever body part he uses.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
A pole in the body fold of a zav,
and he moved a pure person with it — he is pure.
A pole in the body fold of a pure person,
and he moved the zav with it — he is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, still about body folds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זב who moves a pure person with a pole in his body fold does not make him impure. A pure person who moves a זב with a pole in his own fold does become impure.

steps.title: The פסוק that teaches the זב's impurity by moving
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the first case is pure. It begins answering with a פסוק that it reads as speaking about the זב's הסט, a kind of טומאה found nowhere else in the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because the פסוק says: 'And whoever the זב touches without having rinsed his hands in water.' This refers to the זב's moving, a type of impurity we do not find anywhere else in the whole תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind ריש לקיש's first ruling. It starts the answer by bringing a פסוק as the source of the זב's הסט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse uses the word 'touches.' But the גמרא reads it as teaching הסט, which is a unique impurity found only by a זב. This sets up the next step, which explains why the verse uses touching language.

keyTerms.meaning: Moving something without direct contact; a way a זב passes on טומאה

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because the verse says:
"And whoever the zav touches,
and he has not rinsed his hands in water" —
this is the moving of a zav,
for we have not found impurity like it
in the entire Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for and begins to give the source behind ריש לקיש's first ruling.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a זב who moves something with a pole in his body fold does not make it impure
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 15:11, read as speaking about the הסט of a זב

steps.title: Moving is like his hands, so it must be from the outside of the body
steps.stepSummary: The תורה described הסט using the language of touch and linked it to the זב's hands. Hands are on the outside of the body, so הסט only counts when done with the outer parts of the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah expressed it in the language of touching, to teach that moving and touching are like his hands. Just as there it is from the outside, so too here it must be from the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its reason. Because the Torah links הסט to the זב's hands, הסט only works with the outer body, not from inside a fold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse calls הסט 'touching' and mentions hands, so הסט is compared to touching with the hands. Hands are an outer body part, so this impurity only comes from the outside of the body. A pole held in a body fold is moved from a hidden, inner place, so the pure person stays טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One (the Torah) expressed it

steps.whatToRemember: A זב's הסט works only with the outer parts of his body, just like touching with his hands. Moving something with a pole held in a body fold does not make it impure.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the first case of ריש לקיש. It also shows that a body fold counts as a hidden, inner place for the זב's הסט.

phrases.english: And the Merciful One expressed it in the language of touching,
to say that moving and touching are like his hands,
just as there it is from the outside,
phrases.notes: 'There' means touching with the hands, which are on the outside of the body.

phrases.english: so too here it is from the outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the reason started in step 3 by explaining why the verse uses touching language.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a זב who moves something with a pole in his body fold does not make it impure
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The Torah compares הסט to touching with the hands. Hands are on the outside of the body, so הסט only counts from the outer body, and a body fold is not the outer body.

steps.title: Sources that a זב and בעל קרי are only impure once the flow leaves the body
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that a זב and a בעל קרי are not טמא until the flow comes out, and gives a פסוק for each.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: but a זב and a בעל קרי do not become impure until the flow comes out. For a זב, the פסוק says 'when he has a flow from his flesh', meaning it must come out of his flesh. For a בעל קרי, the פסוק says 'when seed goes out from him'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section. It quotes the next line of the משנה and shows where in the Torah each part of that rule comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman becomes טמא even when blood only reaches the inside of her body. A זב and a בעל קרי are different. Both פסוקים use 'from' language (מבשרו, ממנו), and the גמרא reads this to mean the flow must actually leave the body.

keyTerms.meaning: A man with an unusual discharge that makes him טמא
A man who had an emission of seed
From his flesh, meaning out of his body

phrases.english: But the זב and one who had an emission
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה, which first said a woman is טמא even when the blood is still inside her.

phrases.english: do not become impure, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' stands for the rest of the משנה's line: not until the flow comes out.

phrases.english: A זב, as it is written:
'When he has a flow from his flesh'
not until his flow comes out of his flesh.
One who had an emission, as it is written:
'And if seed goes out from a man.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל הַזָּב וּבַעַל קֶרִי אֵינָן מְטַמְּאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the הסט discussion and goes back to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זב and a בעל קרי become טמא only once the flow leaves the body, as the פסוקים say 'from his flesh' and 'goes out from him'.

steps.title: May a person hold his אמה? A ברייתא says it is a terrible act
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a כהן who feels an emission coming holds his אמה. The גמרא challenges this from רבי אליעזר, who compares holding the אמה while urinating to bringing a flood on the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if he was eating תרומה and felt an emission coming, he holds his אמה. Can he really hold it? A ברייתא teaches that רבי אליעזר says: anyone who holds his אמה while urinating is as if he brings a flood to the world!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a כהן eating תרומה. It then attacks the idea that he may hold his אמה, using a ברייתא that strongly condemns doing so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to allow, and even advise, holding the אמה so the כהן can finish his תרומה while still טהור. But רבי אליעזר treats holding the אמה as an extremely serious sin, because touching it can bring on an emission. So how can the משנה allow it?

keyTerms.meaning: The holy portion of produce given to a כהן, which he may only eat while טהור
He felt, here meaning he felt an emission about to happen

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה is not allowing touching for its own sake. The כהן holds the אמה only to keep the seed from coming out, so he can stay טהור while he swallows the תרומה.

phrases.english: If he was eating תרומה and felt, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה continues: he holds his אמה to stop the emission and swallows the תרומה.

phrases.english: He holds?!
But a ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר says:
Anyone who holds his אמה and urinates
is as if he brings a flood to the world!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next case in the משנה and challenges it right away.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's instruction that the כהן holds his אמה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא calls holding the אמה as bad as bringing a flood, so how can the משנה allow it?

steps.title: אביי: he holds it with a thick cloth
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the משנה means holding the אמה through a thick cloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: the משנה means he holds it with a thick cloth.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by saying the משנה and the ברייתא are talking about different ways of holding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא forbids holding the אמה directly. A thick cloth does not cause any stimulation, so it can be used to stop the emission without the danger the ברייתא warns about.

phrases.english: אביי said:
With a thick cloth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי אליעזר's ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case: the משנה is talking about holding through a thick cloth
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to allow plain holding, which the ברייתא forbids
steps.terutzMaskana: Holding through a thick cloth is allowed, because it causes no stimulation

steps.title: רבא: even a soft cloth, since the seed is already loose
steps.stepSummary: רבא says even a soft cloth is allowed, because once the seed has broken loose, holding does not change anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: you can even say the משנה means a soft cloth. Once the seed has broken loose, it is already loose.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer to the same challenge, one that allows even a soft cloth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא forbids holding because it can cause an emission. Here the seed has already broken loose, so holding cannot cause anything new. It only keeps the seed from coming out.

keyTerms.meaning: Once it has broken loose, it is already loose

phrases.english: רבא said:
You can even say with a soft cloth,
since once it has broken loose, it is loose.
phrases.notes: He means the seed has already moved from its place, so holding cannot make a new emission happen.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בְּמַטְלִית רַכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer that is more lenient than אביי's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the ברייתא's danger does not apply in the משנה's case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any holding of the אמה seemed forbidden, or at least anything softer than a thick cloth
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the seed is already loose, even holding with a soft cloth adds nothing and is allowed

steps.title: The root of the disagreement between אביי and רבא
steps.stepSummary: אביי worries that a soft cloth may add to the emission. רבא does not have this worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי is concerned that perhaps he will come to add more seed. רבא is not concerned about adding more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly why אביי and רבא gave different answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree the seed is already loose. The question is whether a soft cloth might stimulate him and cause even more seed to come. אביי fears this, so he requires a thick cloth. רבא does not fear it, so he allows a soft one.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי: only a thick cloth, out of concern for adding more seed. רבא: even a soft cloth, since the seed is already loose and he does not fear adding more.

phrases.english: And אביי is concerned
that perhaps he will come to add more,
and רבא is not concerned about adding more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the two answers in steps 7 and 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The two answers differ over one point: whether a soft cloth might cause more seed to come out.

steps.title: A ברייתא against רבא: like a finger in the eye
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא with a ברייתא saying holding is like a finger in the eye, which keeps making it tear.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: what is this like? It is like someone who puts a finger in his eye. As long as the finger is in the eye, the eye tears and tears again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to go against רבא. This sets up a challenge that the גמרא will deal with next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said holding does not add to the seed. The ברייתא compares holding to a finger in the eye: the touching itself keeps causing more flow. That sounds just like אביי's worry, and it seems to disprove רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this like? A phrase that opens a comparison

phrases.english: But a ברייתא teaches: what is this like?
Like one who puts a finger in the eye,
for as long as the finger is in the eye,
it tears, and tears again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's position from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that holding, even with a soft cloth, does not add to the emission
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says holding is like a finger in the eye, which keeps causing more flow. So holding does add, just as אביי feared.

steps.title: רבא: a second heating at that moment is uncommon
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the finger-in-the-eye challenge. Once the seed has already broken loose, a second heating at that same moment is uncommon, so holding will not add to the emission.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא would answer: a heating of the body, and then another heating at that same time, is not common.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge from the ברייתא in step 10. He explains why holding with a soft cloth does not cause more emission in our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's 'finger in the eye' talks about a case where holding stirs the body and causes more emission. רבא says that in our case the body is already in the middle of one heating, because the seed has broken loose. It is unusual for a second heating to start right then, so the soft cloth will not cause any more emission.

keyTerms.meaning: a heating up (arousal) of the body
is not common, does not usually happen

steps.whatToRemember: אביי worries that a soft cloth adds to the emission. רבא holds that once the seed has broken loose, a second heating right then is too uncommon to worry about.

phrases.english: And רבא would say: any heating up of the body
phrases.notes: He means: once the seed has already broken loose and the limbs are shaking.

phrases.english: followed by another heating at that same time is not common.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא, כֹּל אִחֲמוֹמֵי וַהֲדַר אִחֲמוֹמֵי בְּשַׁעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's challenge against רבא from step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ברייתא to a different case: one without a full heating of the body. Once a heating has already uprooted the seed, a second heating right then is uncommon.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to show that holding always causes more emission, so even רבא should forbid a soft cloth.
steps.terutzMaskana: After the seed has broken loose, a second heating at that moment is uncommon, so רבא still allows a soft cloth.

steps.title: שמואל: only seed felt by the whole body makes one impure
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that שכבת זרע which the whole body does not feel does not make a person impure. He learns this from the words 'שכבת זרע', which mean seed that is fit to cause a pregnancy.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: any שכבת זרע that a person's whole body does not feel does not make him impure. Why? The תורה says 'שכבת זרע', which means seed that is fit to make a child.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a rule from שמואל about when an emission of seed makes a man impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה uses the words 'שכבת זרע', seed. שמואל reads this as seed that can actually cause a pregnancy. Seed like that comes out with a feeling through the whole body, so an emission without that feeling does not count for טומאה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule for the rest of the section: feeling is what makes an emission of seed count for טומאה.

phrases.english: שמואל said: any emission of seed

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין כׇּל גּוּפוֹ מַרְגִּישׁ בָּהּ אֵינָהּ מְטַמְּאָה.
phrases.english: that his whole body does not feel does not make him impure.
What is the reason? The תורה said 'an emission of seed',
meaning seed that is fit to cause a pregnancy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כׇּל שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע שֶׁאֵין כׇּל גּוּפוֹ מַרְגִּישׁ בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion about holding the אמה ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An emission of seed that the whole body does not feel does not make a person impure, because the תורה speaks of seed fit to cause a pregnancy.

steps.title: Challenge: woke up warm after thoughts at night
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל from a case where a man had thoughts at night, woke up, and found his body warm. He is impure, even though he did not notice any feeling.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: if a man was having thoughts at night, and he got up and found his flesh warm, he is impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's rule with a source that says the man is impure even though he did not feel the emission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the man only finds out afterward that there was an emission. He was not aware of feeling it. If he is still impure, this seems to show that feeling is not needed, which goes against שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: his flesh is warm, a sign of an emission

phrases.english: They challenged: if he was having thoughts at night,
and he got up and found his flesh warm, he is impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's rule from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that an emission the whole body does not feel does not make a person impure.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The man did not notice any feeling, yet the source calls him impure, so feeling should not be required.

steps.title: רב הונא: he dreamed of relations, which always comes with feeling
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that the case is about a man who dreamed he was having relations. That always comes with feeling, even if he does not remember it when he wakes up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא explained it: this is about someone who had relations in his dream, because it is impossible to have relations without feeling.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the challenge by explaining what the case is really talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man in the source did feel the emission. He just was not aware of it when he woke up, because he dreamed of relations, and relations always come with feeling. So the case fits שמואל's rule: there was feeling, and that is why he is impure.

keyTerms.meaning: he explained it, he read the source as

phrases.aramaic: תַּרְגְּמַאּ רַב הוּנָא: בִּמְשַׁמֵּשׁ מִטָּתוֹ בַּחֲלוֹמוֹ,
phrases.english: רב הונא explained it: it is about one who had relations in his dream,
since it is impossible to have relations without feeling.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְגְּמַאּ רַב הוּנָא: בִּמְשַׁמֵּשׁ מִטָּתוֹ בַּחֲלוֹמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 by explaining the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the case of the source more narrowly.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The man was impure without any feeling at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: He dreamed of relations, so there was certainly feeling, even though he did not notice it. This fits שמואל.

steps.title: Another version: only seed shot like an arrow makes one impure
steps.stepSummary: A second version of שמואל's rule: שכבת זרע that does not shoot out like an arrow does not make a person impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: שמואל said, any שכבת זרע that does not shoot out like an arrow does not make a person impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different way of reporting שמואל's rule. This sets up the next question about how the two versions differ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first version said the whole body must feel the seed. This version says the seed must come out with force, like an arrow. Both seem similar, so the גמרא will next ask where they actually lead to different results.

phrases.english: Another version: שמואל said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹרֶה כְּחֵץ אֵינָהּ מְטַמְּאָה.
phrases.english: any emission of seed that does not shoot out like an arrow does not make one impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the rule from step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seed that does not shoot out like an arrow does not make a person impure.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two versions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two versions of שמואל's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference is there between this version and that version?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question to find the case where the two versions give different rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions need some kind of feeling or force, so they look the same. The גמרא wants a real case where one version says impure and the other says pure.

phrases.english: What difference is there between this version
and that version?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין הַאי לִישָּׁנָא לְהַאי לִישָּׁנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the version in step 15 with the version in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two versions of שמואל's rule lead to different rulings.

steps.title: The difference: loosened with feeling, came out without
steps.stepSummary: The two versions differ when the seed broke loose with a feeling but came out without a feeling.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: when the seed broke loose with a feeling, but came out without a feeling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by giving the one case where the two versions disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the first version, the feeling when the seed broke loose is enough, so he is impure. By the second version, the seed has to shoot out like an arrow as it leaves the body. Here it came out without a feeling, so he is pure.

keyTerms.meaning: there is a difference between them
broke loose, was uprooted (from its place in the body)

steps.whatToRemember: Version 1 (whole body feels it): a feeling when the seed breaks loose is enough to make him impure. Version 2 (shot like an arrow): the seed must also come out with force, so seed that came out without feeling is pure.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two moments. 'Breaking loose' happens inside the body. 'Coming out' is when the seed leaves the body. The versions disagree only when there is a feeling at the first moment but not at the second.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them:
where it broke loose with a feeling and came out without a feeling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two versions differ when the seed broke loose with a feeling but came out without one. The first version says impure; the 'arrow' version says pure.

steps.title: What was obvious to שמואל is a question for רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the case from step 17 was clear to שמואל, but רבא asked about it: seed that broke loose with a feeling and came out without one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Something that was obvious to שמואל was a question for רבא. רבא asked: if the seed broke loose with a feeling but came out without a feeling, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the exact case where שמואל's two versions differ was an open question for רבא. Then it quotes רבא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל the case had a clear answer, whichever version of his rule you follow. רבא did not know whether the feeling at the moment the seed broke loose is enough, or whether a feeling is needed when it actually comes out. The next steps try to answer him.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a question, an open problem
It broke loose, was uprooted, from its place inside the body

phrases.english: A matter that is obvious to Shmuel
phrases.notes: This is the case from step 17, where שמואל's two versions give different answers. Either way, he had an answer.

phrases.english: is a question for Rava.
As Rava asked:
If it broke loose with a feeling
and came out without a feeling, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: מילתא דפשיטא ליה לשמואל מיבעיא ליה לרבא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the case that split the two versions in step 17 and shows that רבא treated it as an open question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does seed that broke loose with a feeling but came out without one make a person impure?

steps.title: Proof from one who immersed before urinating
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to answer רבא from a source: a בעל קרי who immersed without urinating first becomes impure when he later urinates.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a בעל קרי who immersed but did not urinate first becomes impure when he does urinate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to answer רבא's question. Leftover seed comes out with the urine without any feeling, and he is still impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seed that comes out with the urine broke loose earlier with a feeling, but it comes out now without one. Since he is impure, it seems that a feeling when the seed broke loose is enough. That would answer רבא: he is impure.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who had an emission of seed and became impure

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who had an emission and immersed
and did not urinate,
when he urinates, he is impure.
phrases.notes: Some leftover seed comes out together with the urine, and he does not feel it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer רבא's question from step 18.
steps.raayaObject: That seed which broke loose with a feeling but came out without one makes a person impure.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of a בעל קרי who immersed before urinating and becomes impure when he later urinates.

steps.title: There most of the seed came out with a feeling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: in that case most of the seed already came out with a feeling.
steps.simpleTranslation: That case is different, because most of the seed already came out with a feeling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from step 19, so רבא's question stays open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the בעל קרי case, the main emission came out with a feeling, and the small leftover just follows it. In רבא's case, maybe all the seed came out without a feeling. So the בעל קרי case does not tell us the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there; a phrase used to push away a proof

phrases.english: It is different there,
since most of it came out with a feeling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof only, not the ruling about the בעל קרי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof case is not the same: there most of the seed came out with a feeling, unlike רבא's case.

steps.title: Another version: weak seed cannot cause pregnancy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another version of שמואל's statement: seed that does not shoot like an arrow cannot cause pregnancy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it another way. שמואל said: any seed that does not shoot out like an arrow cannot cause pregnancy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of שמואל's words. In this version he is talking about pregnancy, not impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 15, שמואל's rule was about impurity: seed that does not shoot like an arrow does not make a person impure. Here the same words are about whether the seed can make a woman pregnant. The next step shows what this means for impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: Shoots out like an arrow, with force

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 15. There, weak seed does not make a person impure. In this version, weak seed only cannot cause pregnancy, and the next step says it does make a person impure.

phrases.english: Some say it in another version:
Shmuel said:
Any seed
that does not shoot out like an arrow
cannot cause pregnancy.

steps.triggerLanguage: לישנא אחרינא אמרי לה אמר שמואל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of שמואל's statement from the one discussed in steps 15 to 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seed that does not shoot out like an arrow cannot cause pregnancy.

steps.title: It still makes a person impure, based on a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא learns from שמואל's wording that weak seed still makes a person impure, and supports this with a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: It only cannot cause pregnancy, but it does make a person impure. The פסוק says: "If there is among you a man who is not pure because of an occurrence," which means any emission at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads שמואל's words carefully and concludes that weak seed is still impure. Then it brings a פסוק to back this up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל only said the seed cannot cause pregnancy, so he did not say it is pure. The פסוק uses the general word מקרה, which includes any emission, even a weak one that cannot cause pregnancy.

keyTerms.meaning: It does make a person impure
Because of an occurrence, meaning an emission of seed

steps.whatToRemember: In this version of שמואל, weak seed that does not shoot like an arrow cannot cause pregnancy, but it still makes a person impure.

phrases.english: It is only to cause pregnancy that it cannot,
but to make impure, it does make impure,
as it says:
"If there is among you a man
who is not pure because of an occurrence"
even any emission at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אזרועי הוא דלא מזרעא הא טמויי מטמיא שנאמר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the impurity ruling out of the version of שמואל's words given in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: That seed which does not shoot like an arrow still makes a person impure.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 23:11, where the word מקרה includes any emission.

steps.title: A גוי who had thoughts and then immersed to convert
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks about a גוי who had thoughts, so seed broke loose inside him, and who then immersed to convert.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: a גוי had thoughts, then went down and immersed. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks a new question that is like his earlier one. Seed broke loose while he was a גוי, and it comes out after he has become a Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גוי does not become impure through seed, but a Jew does. Here the seed broke loose while he was a גוי, and it comes out after he immersed and converted. The question is whether that seed makes him impure now.

keyTerms.meaning: He had thoughts, here meaning thoughts that cause seed to break loose
He went down and immersed, here to convert

phrases.english: Rava asked:
A non-Jew who had thoughts,
and went down and immersed
phrases.notes: He immersed to convert. Afterward, the seed that broke loose earlier comes out.

phrases.english: what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question by רבא, built like his question in step 18: the seed broke loose in one situation and came out in another.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does seed that broke loose while he was a גוי, and came out after he converted, make him impure?

steps.title: The two sides of the convert question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the convert case is a real doubt. Maybe 'we follow the moment it broke loose' only applies when it makes things stricter, and here it would make things more lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say that we go by the moment the seed broke loose, maybe that is only when it leads to a stricter ruling. But here it would lead to a lenient ruling, so maybe we don't say it. Or maybe there is no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is laying out the two sides of רבא's question from Step 23 about the גוי who converted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words אם תמצי לומר mean the גמרא only grants, for the sake of argument, that we go by the moment of עקירה. It was never proven, since the proof in step 19 was pushed away in step 20. For a born Jew that rule would be strict, but for the convert it would make him pure, because at that moment he was still a גוי, so the question is whether the rule, even if granted, works only לחומרא or in every case.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say: the גמרא grants one side and still finds room for doubt
We go by the moment of uprooting, when the discharge broke loose inside the body

steps.confusionAlert: Here, going 'by the moment it broke loose' makes the person PURE, because at that moment he was still a גוי. In the earlier case it made him impure. That flip is the whole point of the question.

phrases.english: Even if you say
that we go by the moment of uprooting,
phrases.notes: At the moment it broke loose he was still a גוי, so this side would make him pure.

phrases.english: that applies only toward stringency,
but here, where it would lead to leniency,
we do not say it.
Or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר בָּתַר עֲקִירָה אָזְלִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two possible sides of the question asked in Step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the rule of following the moment of uprooting apply even when it leads to a lenient result, as with a convert?

steps.title: The convert question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cannot decide the convert question, so it remains open.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the convert question without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means no proof was found for either side. The question stays in doubt, and later authorities must decide how to rule in such a case.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question remains unresolved

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question laid out in Steps 23-24.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether a convert is impure from seed that broke loose before his conversion is left unresolved.

steps.title: A זבה whose urine broke loose before she immersed
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks about a זבה whose urine broke loose inside her before she immersed, but came out only afterward. Is that urine impure?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: a זבה whose urine broke loose, and then she went down and immersed. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new question that applies the same idea of עקירה to a זבה's urine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The urine of a זבה is impure. Here the urine broke loose while she was still a זבה, but it came out only after she immersed and became pure. The question is which moment counts.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who has an irregular flow of blood, outside her normal time, and is impure
Her urine (literally, 'the water of her feet')

phrases.english: רבא asked:
a זבה whose urine broke loose inside her,
and she went down and immersed, what is the law?
phrases.notes: Meaning she urinated only after immersing. Does that urine count as a זבה's urine?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רָבָא: זָבָה שֶׁנֶּעֶקְרוּ מֵימֵי רַגְלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question that uses the same principle of עקירה on a different case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the urine of a זבה that broke loose before her immersion, but came out after it, impure?

steps.title: The two sides of the זבה question
steps.stepSummary: Maybe we follow the moment of uprooting only for seed, which a person cannot hold back. Urine can be held back, so maybe for urine we don't follow the moment it broke loose.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say we go by the moment it broke loose, maybe that is only for seed, which a person cannot hold in. But urine, which she can hold in, maybe not. Or maybe there is no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the זבה case is a real doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seed that broke loose will come out no matter what, so it is treated as if it already left at that moment. Urine can be held in, so breaking loose may not count as leaving the body. The other side says there is no difference between the two.

keyTerms.meaning: Is able to hold it back

phrases.aramaic: אִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר בָּתַר עֲקִירָה אָזְלִינַן,
phrases.english: Even if you say that we go by the moment of uprooting,
that applies only to seed,
which one cannot hold back.
But her urine,
which she can hold back, not.
Or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר בָּתַר עֲקִירָה אָזְלִינַן, הָנֵי מִילֵּי שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two possible sides of the question asked in Step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the rule of following the moment of uprooting apply to urine, which can be held back, or only to seed?

steps.title: The זבה question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: This question is also left without an answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the זבה question without deciding it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source settles whether urine is treated like seed. So the status of the זבה's urine in this case stays in doubt.
steps.whatToRemember: Both of רבא's questions end in תיקו. Each one grants only for the sake of argument that we go by the moment of uprooting ('אם תמצי לומר'). Even then, we do not know if that rule would apply when it makes things lenient (the convert), or to urine, which can be held back (the זבה).

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question laid out in Steps 26-27.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether a זבה's urine that broke loose before her immersion is impure is left unresolved.

steps.title: A gentile זבה whose urine broke loose
steps.stepSummary: רבא begins a new question about a gentile זבה whose urine broke loose inside her. The question continues past this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: a gentile זבה whose urine broke loose...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is setting up a new question that combines the two earlier cases, a convert and a זבה's urine. The rest of the question comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gentile זבה is impure only by rabbinic law. This case mixes the convert idea (a change in status) with the urine idea (something that can be held back). The details of the question follow in the next part of the text.

phrases.english: רבא asked: a gentile זבה
whose urine broke loose inside her,

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רָבָא: גּוֹיָה זָבָה שֶׁנֶּעֶקְרוּ מֵימֵי רַגְלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question that combines the themes of the two previous questions.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the status of urine that broke loose inside a gentile זבה? The full question continues beyond this text.
